breadcrumb: Chapter 1: Statewide Economic Development Strategy & Structural Reform
tldr: Chapter 1 identifies Oregon's fragmented economic development system as a structural barrier to growth. With more than 850 organizations and Business Oregon managing more than 90 legislatively directed programs, the state lacks consistent gubernatorial leadership ('tone at the top') and coordination. Business Oregon operates without clear mandate or political support, making it difficult for businesses to navigate programs or receive coordinated support. The fragmentation constrains Oregon's ability to respond quickly to business needs and time-sensitive investment opportunities.

bullets.text: Oregon's economic development system comprises more than 850 organizations broadly focused on business growth and job creation
Business Oregon manages more than 90 legislatively directed programs
Consistent collaboration around shared priorities is identified as 'the exception, not the norm' in Oregon's system
Business Oregon lacks a clear mandate or sufficient political support to lead a coordinated statewide strategy
System fragmentation prevents businesses from identifying a clear entry point or receiving coordinated support
The state's ability to respond quickly to business needs and time-sensitive investment opportunities is constrained by lack of coordination
Consistent leadership from the governor's office is presented as important for establishing economic development as a priority
